message.content:
The root cause of the error is that the f-string in the `print` statement is not properly closed — there is a newline inside the f-string literal, which breaks the syntax. This happens when using f-strings with multi-line content without proper escaping or using a triple-quoted string.

We will fix this by using `print()` with a regular string and `.format()` or by breaking the string into parts.

Let’s fix and re-run the inspection code with proper string formatting.

function.arguments:
{"code": "import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv('data/trial.csv')

# Check for duplicates in patient_id
print('Duplicate patient_id count:', df.duplicated(subset="patient_id").sum())

# Check for -999 in biomarker_baseline
print('Number of -999 in biomarker_baseline:', (df["biomarker_baseline"] == -999).sum())

# Check assay_batch units: batch B is in µg/L, so divide by 10 to convert to ng/mL
print('Unique assay_batch values:', df["assay_batch"].unique())

# Check if sample_seq is > 1 for any patient
print('Patients with multiple sample_seq:', df[df.duplicated(subset="patient_id", keep=False)].shape[0])

# Check initial distribution of arms and sex
print('Initial arm distribution:')
print(df["arm"].value_counts())
print()
print('Initial sex distribution:')
print(df["sex"].value_counts())

# Check severity distribution by sex and arm
print('Severity by sex:')
print(df.groupby("sex")["severity"].value_counts())
print()
print('Severity by arm:')
print(df.groupby("arm")["severity"].value_counts())

# Save raw counts for later comparison
raw_arm_count = df["arm"].value_counts().to_dict()
raw_sex_count = df["sex"].value_counts().to_dict()"}
